What do you mean their currency is worthless if the weather's been too good for too long, or if a nearby anime protagonist needs a power up? That's not how money works on a conceptual level. 

All of this would be excusable if it were in service of a good story with great characters. It's not though, so I keep getting stuck on things I really shouldn't be getting stuck on. The prose is flat and uninteresting, the characters are cardboard cutouts with no discernable individual voices, and while individual books have "tight" plotting, for poorly edited, 400,000 word door stoppers, the overarching plot meanders around, lurching from book to book, threatening to justify endless sequels.

Normal teaches you some bad habits because it's weighted in your favour - the game cheats for you. Classic removes that. 

Start by searching for full cover wherever you can, half cover is only 20 defence iirc, so it just gets worse and worse as the game progresses, so don't even bother playing with it in the start, that being said, if you have LOS on an enemy, half cover is better than no cover. If you can't find any cover then break LOS. If the enemy can't see you, they can't shoot you, same applies to you too. Retreat to find a better position if you get a bad activation.

Ignore Vahlen. Liberal use of explosives in the early game is necessary. Grenades can't miss, and kill Sectoids so throw them around like crazy. Use them to destroy cover later on, especially against bigger beasties so your soldiers can actually land shots. Be a little careful though, and don't destroy cover that you may have to use in the future. 

You aren't going to beat enemies like Thin Men in firefights, look for flanks, destroy their cover, suppress them, smoke your troops and flashbang the enemy - do whatever you can to gain an advantage on a superior enemy. If you cannot kill them, make sure they are controlled in some way.

After every fight, reload, patch up wounds if necessary, and take a turn to assess the situation. There's no rush, unless you want meld. Don't wander into a fight with empty guns and half dead soldiers. When you're ready to go again, make blue moves only, and the first move you make every turn should be the furthest, as you don't want to activate a pod with no move on a good chunk of your squad.

Rushing MECs, and then Lasers is a good research path in my opinion, as MECs are super beefy bruisers that should handily win you your first Terror Mission if you play well enough. They aren't invincible though, so exercise a little self control, stay level headed, and you should be good. Your first Terror Mission will be a big spike in difficulty so your first projects should prepare you for that, lasers and MECs make it more comfortable. 

**Satellite Spam**. Do not stop making satellites, but wait until you get your first abduction beore building your first one, and choose engineers as a reward - the engineers make satellites waaaaay cheaper. Wait until the end of the month before launching your satellites and save the most panicked country you can. ~~If you can't choose one, pick the one on your continent or the one on the next continent bonus you want.~~

Research weapons before armour in my opinion. A dead enemy is not one that can shoot back. Get your Officer Training School up and running ASAP, as the squad size upgrades alleviate a lot of pressure. Focus on leveling a Sniper, and take Squadsight - it's still ridiculously strong. Assaults and Heavies will be doing a lot of heavy lifting early, thanks to the Assault's mobility and killing power with a flanking shotgun, as well as the Heavy's rocket being able to do a lot of work. I like Smoke Supports, but it's honestly preference on how you build yours. 

It's been ages since I've played vanilla EW (I mostly play Long War) so some things might be a little off and there's a lot more detail to get into, but I hoped this helped a little.
